title: Kahana vs Domestika: When the Course URL Is Not Enough
excerpt: Domestika is course hosting, drip, enrollment, and lesson checkout. Kahana is discovery + cohort discussion around teaching you already run elsewhere.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Originated in Spain; now headquartered in San Francisco/Berkeley, CA.
Thousands of courses across 16+ creative categories (illustration, photography & video, design, craft, 3D & animation, fashion, writing, marketing, and more).
Courses typically USD 10–40 (often discounted); Domestika Plus membership adds credits/perks. One-time purchase = unlimited lifetime access.

strengths.title: High-quality, professionally produced courses
strengths.detail: Courses produced in-house, consistent, well-shot, step-by-step lessons.

strengths.title: Creative-focused content and instructors
strengths.detail: Strong creative disciplines with industry-pro instructors, ideal for illustrators, designers, photographers, crafters.

strengths.title: Lifetime access, self-paced learning
strengths.detail: Purchased courses can be watched forever with unlimited replays and resource access.

strengths.title: Community features
strengths.detail: Each course has a digital community for sharing projects, questions, and feedback from instructors and peers.

weaknesses.title: Language barriers for some learners
weaknesses.detail: Many courses are Spanish with auto-generated subtitles, non-Spanish speakers may rely heavily on subs.

weaknesses.title: Course-only focus (no broader business tools)
weaknesses.detail: No built-in tools for selling digital products, paid communities, or coaching beyond courses.

weaknesses.title: Pricing and subscription confusion
weaknesses.detail: Some users report confusion or dissatisfaction around Domestika Plus vs individual course purchases.

weaknesses.title: Less depth in non-creative subjects
weaknesses.detail: Strength is creative topics; IT and other subjects are thinner than on Udemy or Coursera.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Domestika is course hosting, drip, enrollment, and lesson checkout. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Domestika is an online learning platform for creatives, where the best experts and creatives share their knowledge through professionally produced courses.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Domestika side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Domestika you can use Courses, Memberships, and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with Domestika

You can use both. Domestika keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on Domestika for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. Domestika stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
